edge: Cause two assume-set clock events in one simulation time step.
negative: Require an explicit randomize() call to trigger checker assume-set solving.
positive: Use two assumptions with distinct clocks and trigger solving from each assume-set clock event.

edge: Reference an active variable’s current value while solving.
negative: Solve active free variables after Observed processing begins.
positive: Change an inactive input before Observed and verify solving uses its sampled value and checker properties see solved values.

edge: Exercise the procedural concurrent-assertion treatment of an assertion inside the checker procedure.
positive: Place one immediate, one deferred, and one concurrent assertion in otherwise legal checker always procedures.

negative: Use a timing event control in checker always_comb or always_latch.
positive: Use a legal timing event control in a checker always_ff procedure.

edge: Verify that variables in the always_ff event control are excluded from the sampling rule.
positive: Change an operand around an always_ff event and observe sampled assignment and assertion expressions.
In always_comb and always_latch, observe assignments using current expression values.
Declare and use a let construct in a legal checker always procedure.

edge: Use a loop containing another permitted checker-always statement.
positive: Use a finite for loop in a legal checker always procedure.

edge: Place all three procedure forms in one checker while giving each otherwise legal contents.
positive: Declare one checker procedure of each of the always_comb, always_latch, and always_ff forms.
Use an if statement and a case statement in a legal checker always procedure.

edge: Call a task only where its own timing and argument rules remain legal for the containing always form.
positive: Call a legal function from a checker always procedure.

edge: Use a static function that demonstrably preserves no state.
negative: Call functions having output, inout, or non-const ref arguments.
Call a state-preserving or side-effecting function.
positive: Call an automatic side-effect-free function with input and const-ref arguments from a checker assignment RHS.

edge: Use triggered in the right-hand expression of a permitted nonblocking assignment.
positive: Assign a checker variable from a named sequence’s triggered method.

edge: Use an empty assume set in a procedural checker instance.
negative: Create multiple assume sets for one checker instance.
positive: Instantiate the same checker twice and maintain one independent assume set per instance.

edge: Show that a child instance has its own assume-set membership even when its assumption is excluded from the parent set.
negative: Include an assumption whose referenced formal is connected to a const-cast or automatic actual.
Include an assumption referencing no active free variable.
positive: Include a child-checker assumption whose formal actual depends on an active free variable.

edge: Use an assumption that an implementation also chooses to use for free-variable randomization; runtime violation checking remains required.
negative: Cause a checker assume property to fail and verify that the violation is detected.
positive: Simulate a checker assume statement whose property remains satisfied.

edge: Exercise an unsatisfied or missed solution and permit arbitrary active values while reporting the attempt unsuccessful.
notes: Do not require solver completeness or dead-end avoidance.
positive: Solve an assume set with a readily found satisfying active-variable assignment.

edge: Place the prohibited value in a subexpression rather than as the entire actual.
negative: Use a formal bound to an automatic procedural value in checker procedural code.
Use a formal whose actual contains a const cast in a checker continuous assignment.
positive: Use an automatic procedural actual only in a checker assertion.

edge: Instantiate a checker declared outside the enclosing checker.
positive: Instantiate one checker directly in another checker body.
Place a legal concurrent assertion directly in a checker body.

edge: Override declaration-scope inherited defaults inside the checker.
positive: Declare both default clocking and default disable iff directly in a checker body.
Place a legal deferred assertion directly in a checker body.
Declare and call a legal function directly in a checker body.

edge: Nest a permitted checker declaration inside a checker generate block.
negative: Use a checker generate block to contain an element that would be illegal directly in the checker declaration.
positive: Conditionally generate an assertion or other element permitted directly in a checker body.
Declare and use a let construct directly in a checker body.

edge: Instantiate the nested checker from the enclosing checker.
positive: Declare a checker inside another checker body.
Declare and assert a named property directly in a checker body.
Declare and use a named sequence directly in a checker body.

edge: Use a rand-qualified checker variable with only a permitted assignment form.
positive: Declare a checker variable and update it with a legal assignment form.

edge: Override one context default while inferring another.
negative: Omit such an actual where no legal context value can be inferred.
positive: Use $inferred_clock and $inferred_disable defaults and omit both actuals in a valid context.

edge: Place both the declaration and instance at checker-body scope while sampling variables updated by checker procedures.
negative: Declare or instantiate a covergroup inside a checker initial or always procedure.
positive: Declare and instantiate a covergroup directly in a checker body outside all procedures.

edge: Compare event-triggered sampling with an explicit sample() call while holding the sampled value known.
positive: Call a checker covergroup's sample() from a sequence match item with a known coverpoint value and verify the corresponding bin is sampled.

edge: Contrast const and variable actuals connected to the same covered formal.
negative: Reference in a checker covergroup a formal connected to a const actual.
positive: Cover a checker variable and a formal connected to a non-const actual.

edge: Override inherited default clocking and disable iff contexts inside the checker.
positive: Declare a checker under default clocking and default disable iff contexts and use both without redeclaring them.

edge: Parse both an absent formal-port parenthesis group and an empty parenthesized checker port list.
negative: Omit a required declaration delimiter or use a body token that does not match checker declaration grammar.
positive: Parse a named checker with a formal port, legal body item, and matching optional endchecker identifier.

edge: Give declaration and instantiation scopes different objects with the same name and verify the checker binds the declaration-scope object.
positive: Reference a static variable visible from the checker declaration scope.

edge: Declare a nested checker inside another checker.
negative: Attempt a checker declaration in a procedural block.
positive: Declare one checker in each permitted enclosing scope.

edge: Use $ as the default actual of a nested checker.
negative: Pass $ to a typed formal.
Use the corresponding formal in an arithmetic expression.
positive: Pass $ to an untyped formal used solely as a cycle-delay range upper bound.
Forward a $-bound formal to a nested checker.

edge: Contrast an enclosing static variable with an automatic variable of the same type.
negative: Reference an enclosing automatic variable or an enclosing member or element of a dynamic variable.
positive: Reference a permitted static object from the checker declaration's enclosing scope.

edge: Exercise the restriction separately for fork-join, fork-join_any, and fork-join_none.
negative: Reference an element declared in an enclosing fork block from a checker.
positive: Reference a permitted static object outside the enclosing fork block.

edge: Contrast explicit input without a type with a first formal having neither direction nor type.
negative: Declare input or output explicitly while omitting that formal's type.
positive: Give an explicitly directed checker formal an explicit legal type.

negative: Place a construct in a checker final procedure that is illegal in a non-checker final procedure.
positive: Use an immediate assertion and a legal reporting statement in a checker final procedure.

edge: Compare static and procedural checker instantiations; each instance's final procedure still executes once.
positive: Instantiate a checker twice and count one final-procedure execution per instance at simulation end.

edge: Contrast it with an explicitly directed typeless first formal, which is erroneous.
positive: Declare a first checker formal with neither direction nor type and use it under input-untyped rules.

edge: Distinguish a nested checker declaration from a nested module declaration.
negative: Attempt each of module, interface, program, and package declarations inside a checker.
positive: Declare a nested checker, which is permitted, rather than a forbidden design-unit kind.

edge: Do not infer a package-instantiation case because packages have no corresponding instantiation syntax.
negative: Instantiate a module, interface, or program inside a checker.
positive: Instantiate another checker inside a checker.

edge: Exercise a property-formal-only category on an input checker formal.
negative: Use a checker formal type that is not legal for a property formal.
positive: Declare checker formals using representative data, event, sequence, property, and untyped forms permitted for property formals, subject to output restrictions.

edge: Contrast passing a free actual with declaring the receiving formal free.
negative: Declare a function formal or local variable with the free-variable rand usage prohibited here.
positive: Pass a checker free variable as an actual to a function with an ordinary formal.

edge: Use an event control as the sole permitted procedural timing-control form.
negative: Use a delay control in a checker initial procedure.
positive: Put each permitted assertion kind, a let declaration, and an event control in a checker initial procedure.

edge: Contrast assignment to an output formal with assignment to an otherwise same-typed input formal.
negative: Assign to an input checker formal from checker code.
positive: Read an input checker formal in assertions and expressions without assigning to it.

edge: Override the declared default with an explicit actual.
positive: Give a singular checker input a default and omit its actual at instantiation.

edge: Use identically spelled names in declaration and instantiation scopes to exercise name resolution before substitution.
negative: Pass an actual whose substitution makes a construct in the flattened checker illegal.
positive: Instantiate a checker with an input expression whose substitution leaves the flattened checker legal.

edge: Reach a procedural checker instance conditionally while its non-static-assertion contents continue to exist on unvisited time steps.
positive: Instantiate a checker twice and observe independent internal state persisting across time steps.

edge: Contrast direct nesting in a checker body, which is permitted, with nesting inside that checker's procedure.
negative: Instantiate a checker inside an initial or always procedure belonging to another checker.
positive: Instantiate a checker in an ordinary module procedure at a concurrent-assertion-legal location.

edge: Keep fork-block and another checker's procedure exclusions out of the otherwise permitted location scenario.
positive: Instantiate a checker at representative static and ordinary procedural locations where concurrent assertions are permitted.

negative: Instantiate a checker separately in fork-join, fork-join_any, and fork-join_none blocks.
positive: Instantiate a checker in otherwise legal procedural code outside a fork block.

edge: Use an omitted ordered actual and an empty named actual connection.
negative: Omit a required checker-instantiation delimiter or mix connection tokens outside the grammar alternatives.
positive: Instantiate a package-scoped checker once with ordered property actuals and once with named property actuals.

edge: Combine one wildcard with explicit named checker connections.
negative: Use .* twice in one checker port connection list.
positive: Use one .* wildcard in an otherwise legal named checker connection list.

edge: Use several consecutive omitted types after changing the preceding formal's explicit type.
positive: Declare a typed directionless formal followed by a directionless typeless formal and exercise the inferred type.

edge: Use the same local name in two distinct checker declarations without creating a shared declaration.
negative: Attempt to reference a checker-local type or variable unqualified from the enclosing scope.
positive: Declare a type and variable inside a checker and use them within that checker.

edge: Reach a procedural checker instantiation intermittently while its checker-local state persists.
positive: Update an internal checker variable across clock events and observe its value persist.

edge: Schedule Reactive work and a Re-Inactive event before the checker-variable Re-NBA update.
negative: Apply a checker nonblocking update in Active or Reactive.
positive: Capture a sequence triggered value in a checker nonblocking assignment and observe the checker-variable update in Re-NBA.

edge: Connect to a legal selected lvalue.
negative: Connect a checker output to a non-lvalue expression.
positive: Connect checker outputs to a variable lvalue and a net lvalue.

edge: Use a sequence-typed input formal as a contrast to the prohibited sequence-typed output.
negative: Declare checker outputs separately as untyped, sequence, and property.
positive: Declare a checker output using a legal explicit data type.

edge: Use the same syntactic placement for an input default and an output initial value while observing their distinct semantics.
positive: Give a singular checker output an initial value and observe it before subsequent checker updates.

edge: Use always_comb, always_latch, and always_ff only under the specialized form and content rules that follow in 17.5.
positive: Place an otherwise legal initial procedure, always procedure, and final procedure in a checker body.

edge: Use an implicit named connection where the matching actual is visible in the instantiation scope.
positive: Instantiate equivalent checkers using positional, explicit named, and implicit named connections.

edge: Omit the first formal's direction and verify it defaults to input, then change direction explicitly for later inheritance.
positive: Omit directions on formals following an explicit output and verify they inherit output.

edge: Use a checker continuous assignment and a blocking statement in the same time step.
negative: Execute a change-sensitive checker construct or checker blocking statement in Active rather than Reactive.
positive: Trigger a checker blocking statement from a clock change and distinguish its Reactive execution from design Active execution.

edge: Use a nonblocking assignment in each checker always form subject to that form's general rules.
negative: Use a blocking assignment in checker always_ff.
positive: Assign ordinary checker variables using continuous assignment, blocking assignment in always_comb or always_latch, and nonblocking assignment in always_ff.

edge: Contrast hierarchical reading in a nonassignment context with hierarchical use in an assignment.
negative: Assign a checker instance variable through its hierarchical name from enclosing code.
positive: Assign a checker variable from within its checker using an unqualified name.

edge: Compare declaration initialization with an equivalent initial assignment.
negative: Assign a checker variable in a checker initial procedure.
positive: Initialize a checker variable in its declaration.

edge: Distinguish a checker formal from a checker-body net declaration.
negative: Declare a net in a checker body.
positive: Declare and use an ordinary variable in a checker body.

edge: Use sampled values and an action block to expose scheduling equivalence.
negative: Schedule the checker-contained assertion in a checker-specific region.
positive: Run equivalent concurrent assertions inside a checker and directly in design code and compare scheduling-visible results.

edge: Contrast rand const with a non-const rand checker variable.
positive: Declare both initialized and uninitialized rand const checker variables.

edge: Use an empty assume set explicitly and by absence of assumptions.
negative: Change that value again before the end of the same time step.
positive: Use an active free variable with an empty assume set and permit a new random value each time step.

edge: Compare otherwise equivalent rand and non-rand checker variables.
positive: Declare a rand checker variable and use it in an assumption.

edge: Contrast packed aggregate classification with separate unpacked-element classification.
negative: Treat an assigned free variable or checker formal as active.
positive: Randomize an unassigned non-const free variable as active.

edge: Apply each assignment form to otherwise identical free and non-free checker variables.
negative: Continuously assign a free checker variable.
Use a blocking procedural assignment to a free checker variable.
positive: Assign a free checker variable using a nonblocking assignment.

edge: Constrain the free variable to a singleton allowed behavior.
negative: Collapse an unconstrained free checker variable to one fixed formal behavior.
positive: Constrain a const or non-const free checker variable to several allowed behaviors and verify formal analysis retains all of them.

edge: Initialize one element explicitly while leaving a separately classified element uninitialized.
negative: Replace an explicit declaration initializer with an unconstrained random value.
positive: Observe initialization of active, inactive, const, and non-const uninitialized free variables.

edge: Use assumptions that restrict, but do not uniquely determine, allowed non-const values.
negative: Treat an uninitialized non-const free variable as permanently fixed or rerandomize a const free variable after initialization.
positive: Simulate const and non-const free checker variables and exercise their respective random assignment events under 17.7.2.

edge: Have another assume-set event occur within the same time step and permit a new solved value then.
negative: Change a solved free variable before another assume-set event or time-step end.
positive: Solve a free variable and observe it remain fixed until the next assume-set event.

edge: Compare against a non-const free variable with the same declaration initializer.
negative: Change an initialized constant free variable after initialization.
positive: Initialize a rand const checker variable and observe the declared value throughout simulation.

edge: Use multiple levels of statically nested checkers under one procedural top-level instance.
positive: Statically nest a checker with concurrent and deferred assertions, then instantiate the top-level checker procedurally.

edge: Add a declaration initializer and restrict only the first formal time step to it.
negative: Permanently fix an unassigned non-const free variable to one formal value.
positive: Leave a non-const free variable uninitialized and retain all possible values at every formal time step.

edge: Compare with an uninitialized non-const free variable, which is unconstrained or randomized from the first step.
negative: Ignore or replace the declared initializer at the first time step.
positive: Initialize an otherwise unassigned non-const free variable and observe the initializer at the first time step.

edge: Instantiate the checker statically, but place the assertion itself inside a checker procedure; verify that the assertion remains procedural rather than acquiring the static-assertion treatment used elsewhere in the same checker.
notes: Use the queueing, maturation, and clock-inference rules owned by 16.14.6 for the runtime oracle.
positive: Place a concurrent assertion in an always procedure inside a checker and reach it before its leading clock event; exercise the procedural assertion queue and subsequent clocked evaluation.

edge: Reach the instance and then trigger a procedural assertion flush point before maturation.
positive: Reach a procedural checker instance and allow its static concurrent assertion to mature from the procedural assertion queue.

edge: Reach the instance and then flush the pending deferred assertion report under the procedural deferred-assertion rules.
positive: Reach a procedural checker instance and allow its static deferred assertion report to mature.

edge: Use nonmatching time steps before the first matching clock event and verify no assertion attempt begins there.
negative: Require procedural visitation before monitoring a static checker concurrent assertion.
positive: Statically instantiate a checker and trigger its static concurrent assertion on a matching initial clock event.

edge: Change the expression without any concurrent assertion clock event.
negative: Require a concurrent assertion clock event before monitoring the changed deferred expression.
positive: Statically instantiate a checker and change a static deferred assertion's expression to trigger monitoring.

edge: Contrast its fixed chosen value with per-time-step values of an uninitialized non-const free variable.
negative: Allow an uninitialized constant free variable to change after its initialization value is chosen.
positive: Leave a rand const checker variable uninitialized and observe one value remain fixed.

edge: Contrast with an implicitly clocked active variable in an empty assume set.
positive: Place one active free variable outside all properties of a nonempty assume set and update it at each set event.

edge: Use multiple assume properties with different clocks after one unsuccessful attempt.
negative: Report assumption failure immediately at solution-attempt time before the property is checked.
positive: Force an unsuccessful solution and observe failure only at the unsatisfied property’s Observed-region check.
